rationale_by_leg.zai-glm-5p2: Two strongest stories nailed and meticulously sourced: repeatedly flags single-primary-source and unfetched primaries, treats the 30-day framework as single-source/unconfirmed, and offers a real counter-reading (the asks 'function like a ban'). Verify chips match the evidence. Misses the major Microsoft/CyberGym story and Google $44B. One clear fabrication: the Skeptic's-corner 'Anthropic-5.5 leak' cites @Amank1412 with a URL that actually belongs to @rauchg's Kimi K3 tweet; no such account or leak exists in the snapshot, though it is hedged 'unverified rumor.' Overall the most trustworthy brief to ship.
rationale_by_leg.claude: Broader, punchy coverage — captures Microsoft/CyberGym (all numbers accurate), Google $44B, and Kimi K3 arena. But more and worse faithfulness failures: Story 3 attributes the announcement to @satyanadella/@mustafasuleyman tweet IDs that don't exist (real sources: WesRoth/rohanpaul/testingcatalog), and the headline reuses the fake @satyanadella URL. Story 2 launders a single-source (The Information) item into '✓ multi-source confirmed' via a fabricated 'Fortune via @leomschwartz' citation, and asserts an 'Aug 1 deadline / June executive order' with zero snapshot support. Distorted verification status undercuts a news brief's core value.
